description:

It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture. Role overview: This role plays a key part in protecting Haleon’s digital environment and keeping our business secure every day. As a Senior Cyber Security Analyst, you will be at the forefront of detecting and responding to cyber threats, identifying vulnerabilities, reducing risk, and helping safeguard the systems and data that support millions of consumers worldwide. You will investigate security alerts, assess potential threats, and lead incidents through to resolution using a variety of cutting-edge security tools and technologies. Success in this role requires both strong analytical thinking and hands-on technical expertise, with the ability to quickly understand a situation, select the right approach, and take effective action. As a Senior member of the team, you will work across a broad range of security scenarios, making a real impact on Haleon’s cyber resilience while collaborating with experienced professionals in a global security environment. Ready to take on meaningful cyber security challenges and help shape the defence of a global organisation? We'd love to hear from you. Apply today or reach out to learn more about the opportunity. Key responsibilities: Operate as part of a 24 /7 Cyber Security Operations (SecOps) team that continuously monitors the security of the company. Undertake the timely triage of security alerts to allow for rapid incident detection and response. Perform deep-dive analysis of security events, logs, network traffic and forensic data to determine root cause, identifying suspicious and / or anomalous activities and taking appropriate action based on documented processes and procedures. Recommended modifications to internal defences and processes for more effective and efficient security operations. Manage security incidents through all phases of the incident response lifecycle from identification through to closure. Ensures that delegated response and remediation actions are completed in line with SLAs. Provides expert analytic investigative support of complex security incidents. Supports the tuning of all security tooling and the development of bespoke correlation rules / use cases aligned to business operations, internal risk profiles and current threat intelligence. Ensure that the automation and orchestration of day-to-day operations is maximised, and that analysis / response activities are performed as efficiently as possible. Execute L2/L3 event or incident response and investigations into suspicious activity. Shape the operations to successfully manage cases, lead the response process, and delegate tasks to junior incident responders and MSSP analysts. Generate post-incident reviews to ensure gaps are closed to prevent future events. Collaborate with Threat Intelligence to groom threat feeds and help translate findings. Help prioritize content, develop, and implement playbooks and runbooks. Be a key member of the Cyber Incident Response Team (CIRT) during major cyber incidents. Establish and maintain relationships with other investigation and remediation teams within the company, working closely with them to address the full spectrum of security issues. Lead efforts in developing security awareness training for the broader organisation. Your profile Required: 5+ years of experience in cyber security, including security monitoring, incident response, and threat investigation. 3+ years of working experience in a Cyber Security Operations Centre (SOC). Hands-on experience managing and investigating complex cyber incidents, including advanced attacks, ransomware events, and targeted threat activity. Understanding of security controls and how they are used to detect and respond. Ability to communicate complex problems succinctly. Ability to work within a team environment, sharing workload and responsibility. Preferred: Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security or related field (or equivalent experience). Experience working across international manufacturing. Knowledge of common network protocols, edge routing technologies, firewall/IDS/IPS, SIEM, EDR/XDR. CISSP, GCIA, GCDA, GSOC, GCIH. Why Haleon? None of us should ever feel like we’re standing still. At Haleon, we want you to feel supported, valued, and always progressing. Improving everyday health takes dedication, energy, and effort — so we reward your contribution with a benefits package that includes: Contract of employment Company car or car allowance according to car policy LTI Long Term Incentive Annual bonus that reflects performance Fully on-site role with on-call duties (weekends) Private medical package (Medicover) with additional preventive healthcare services for employees and their eligible Multisport card or points on the Multicafeteria Benefits account Health and wellbeing programmes that take care of you physically and mentally Pension plan membership and savings programme (PPE) Personalized learning paths and access to diverse development tools to support your professional growth. Generali Life insurance Supportive community and integration events Family benefits (extra parental leave, caregiver’s policy) Free car and bike parking

title: Head of Enterprise Service Platforms & Transformation
description: Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. Role Summary The Head of Enterprise Service Platforms & Transformation is defining and delivering the enterprise service management and intelligent operations strategy, enabling a modern, automated, data-driven and user-centric service experience across the organisation. This leader will drive enterprise service transformation by bringing together people, process, data and technology to simplify cross-functional user journeys, improve operational resilience, increase automation, strengthen service intelligence and maximise the value of strategic technology investments. Key responsibilities Enterprise Service Platform & Product Ownership Act as the enterprise product owner for ServiceNow, accountable for strategy, roadmap, investment prioritisation, platform value realisation and measurable business outcomes. Working in conjunction with key stakeholders, own the configuration and governance of ServiceNow across all enterprise modules and future enterprise workflows. Establish and lead a ServiceNow Centre of Excellence, ensuring consistent platform standards, architecture, configuration principles and governance. Manage enterprise portfolio demand and prioritisation across business functions, balancing innovation, simplification, scalability and platform integrity. Drive adoption of new platform capability, including workflow automation, AI, predictive intelligence and intelligent service experiences. Maximise return on ServiceNow investment through effective licensing, adoption, optimisation and capability utilisation. Service Data Strategy, Foundations & Quality Own the enterprise strategy for foundational service data, ensuring it is trusted, governed, complete, accurate and fit for purpose. Define and implement clear data ownership, stewardship, accountability and governance models across service and technology domains. Establish enterprise standards for service taxonomy, service ownership, service models, asset relationships and configuration data. Create a trusted view of business services, applications, infrastructure, dependencies, ownership and operational health. Define and monitor service data quality measures, controls and remediation plans. Embed data ownership and lifecycle management into operational processes and technology delivery. Ensure trusted service data provides the foundation for automation, AI, operational intelligence, risk management, executive reporting and decision-making. CMDB & Service Mapping Own the maturity roadmap for the Configuration Management Database and associated configuration management practices. Improve CMDB completeness, accuracy, governance and operational adoption. Establish clear relationships between business services, applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, technology assets and operational dependencies. Improve discovery, reconciliation, service mapping and lifecycle management capabilities. Ensure the CMDB supports effective incident management, change impact assessment, operational risk management, resilience and cyber controls. Drive the integration of CMDB data with observability, monitoring, automation and operational intelligence capabilities. AIOps, Observability & Intelligent Operations Define and deliver the strategy for AI-enabled operations, supporting the transition from reactive service management to predictive and preventative operations. Improve enterprise observability by integrating monitoring, telemetry, events and service health data across the technology landscape. Establish greater end-to-end visibility of service health, performance and user impact. Drive intelligent event correlation, anomaly detection, root cause identification and automated remediation. Reduce operational noise and manual intervention through event intelligence, automation and self-healing capabilities. Enable early identification of service degradation before it materially impacts users or business operations. Use operational intelligence to improve availability, resilience, service performance and decision-making. Enterprise Process Excellence & User Journey Transformation Establish a process excellence capability with Lean methodologies, value-stream analysis and data-driven continual improvement. Lead the redesign of complex end-to-end processes, designing service experiences around end-to-end user journeys Identify and remove waste, duplication, bottlenecks, unnecessary hand-offs and manual activity. Establish measurable process performance indicators covering efficiency, experience, quality and business outcomes. Drive standardisation where appropriate while ensuring processes remain responsive to genuine business requirements. Service Transformation, Automation & AI Enablement Define and deliver the enterprise service transformation roadmap. Identify and prioritise opportunities for automation, workflow optimisation and AI adoption across enterprise services. Increase self-service, automated fulfilment and intelligent workflow capability. description: Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science. Now it’s time to fully realise the full potential of our business and our people. Role Summary The Head of End User Services & Digital Workplace is the senior accountable leader for the strategy, evolution, performance and end-to-end digital workplace experience for colleagues globally. The role owns a significant enterprise technology portfolio spanning Modern Workplace, End User Computing, Digital Employee Experience, Service Desk and Desk-Side Services, Executive Technology Support, AV and Workplace Technology, end-user device and asset lifecycle management, and associated strategic partners and suppliers. Accountable for both run, evolution and transform, the role will define the future Digital Workplace strategy and multi-year investment roadmap while ensuring existing services remain secure, resilient, performant and cost-effective. The role will establish the standards, operating model, governance and capabilities required to deliver a consistent global employee experience while accommodating legitimate business, geographic and persona-specific requirements. A key leadership mandate is to transform traditional End User Services from a reactive, technology-centric support model into an experience-led, data-driven and increasingly proactive, predictive and autonomous Digital Workplace, using Digital Employee Experience telemetry, observability, AI, automation and self-healing capabilities to prevent and resolve technology friction before it impacts colleagues. The Head of End User Services & Digital Workplace will also ensure that investment in workplace technology, including AI-enabled productivity capabilities, translates into measurable improvements in employee experience, productivity, security, resilience and business value. Key Responsibilities End User Services & Workplace Strategy Own and define the global End User Services and Digital Workplace vision, strategy, target operating model and multi-year transformation roadmap, aligned to enterprise technology strategy security posture and business priorities. Provide strategic leadership across the complete Digital Workplace ecosystem, establishing clear service and capability models, ownership, decision rights, standards and governance. Translate emerging technology, changing employee expectations and evolving ways of working into a coherent workplace technology strategy and investment portfolio. Act as a senior technology advisor to executive and business leadership on Digital Workplace strategy, employee technology experience, investment, risk and emerging capabilities. Maintain awareness of market and technology developments and ensure the organisation continues to benchmark appropriately against leading Digital Workplace practices. End-to-End Service, Product & Experience Ownership Provide end-to-end accountability for the performance, experience, resilience, security, cost and evolution of End User Services and Digital Workplace capabilities. Establish a mature product and service ownership model in which services have clear accountability across strategy, architecture, lifecycle, investment, risk, performance, experience and continual improvement. Ensure accountability extends across internal organisational and external supplier boundaries, eliminating gaps between workplace platforms, infrastructure, networks, identity, cyber security, applications and support organisations. Own the overall employee technology experience and ensure services are designed around business and employee outcomes Establish clear service integration, RACI, dependencies and governance across the complete Digital Workplace ecosystem. Modern Workplace, Engineering & Technology Strategy Provide senior ownership of the Modern Workplace technology ecosystem, including Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, Exchange, endpoint technologies, collaboration, productivity platforms and emerging AI-enabled capabilities. Define the strategic direction, engineering standards, architecture guardrails, platform roadmaps and lifecycle requirements required to provide secure, scalable and resilient workplace services. Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Identity, Data and Platform Engineering to ensure workplace technologies are appropriately architected, secure, supportable and operationally ready. Drive cloud-native and evergreen approaches to workplace technology management, reducing reliance on legacy technologies and traditional large-scale upgrade programmes. Maintain clear visibility of technology currency, lifecycle risk, obsolescence and technical debt, supported by multi-year investment and remediation plans. Ensure innovation is appropriately evaluated and translated into tangible employee and business value AI, Automation & Autonomous Digital Workplace Define and lead the strategy for AI-enabled, automated and increasingly autonomous workplace operations. Lead the workplace technology enablement of enterprise AI productivity capabilities, including Microsoft Copilot and future AI technologies, working with Cyber Security, Data, Architecture and Governance to ensure secure and responsible adoption. Ensure strong governance of endpoint security, vulnerability remediation, patch compliance, security configuration and technology currency. Own Digital Workplace technology risks, audit findings and remediation programmes, ensuring appropriate executive visibility and timely resolution. Own the resilience and continuity of critical workplace services and ensure employees can remain productive during major technology, cyber, site or supplier disruption. Participate in enterprise operational resilience, disaster recovery and cyber-response exercises and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into future service design. Use employee experience, workplace utilisation and technology-performance data to inform future workplace investment. Ensure appropriate resilience and support models exist for executive, high-profile and business-critical collaboration environments. Ensure effective service design and transition into live operation, with appropriate operational readiness, supportability, security and lifecycle considerations. Maintain a measurable continual-improvement portfolio informed by experience, operational, financial, supplier and technology data. Ensure major technology investments have clear adoption and benefits-realisation plans, recognising that technical deployment alone does not constitute success. Establish clear accountability, decision rights and performance expectations across internal teams and strategic partners. Develop organisational capability across Modern Workplace engineering, Digital Employee Experience, AI and automation, workplace technology, observability, analytics and product/service ownership. Ensure appropriate succession planning, talent development and capability strategies exist for critical roles. Create a culture of ownership, customer focus, simplification, innovation, operational excellence and continuous improvement. We do this through our Win as One strategy. It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture. About the role The Mechanical Technician is responsible to troubleshoot, inspect, maintain, repair, and document work on mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment involved in the manufacturing and packaging of pharmaceutical products. Role Responsibilities Observe and test machinery and equipment and analyze information obtained from operators to diagnose malfunctions and equipment problems. Execute preventative maintenance (PM) instructions based on maintenance schedules. Disassemble machinery and equipment to remove parts and make repairs. Examine parts for defects such as breakage and excessive wear. Repair and replace broken and malfunctioning components. Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs. Operate newly repaired machinery and equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs. Record repairs and maintenance performed. Record parts and materials used, and order new parts and materials as necessary. Study blueprints and manufacturers’ manuals to determine correct installation and operation of machinery. Design and machine fixtures, tooling, and experimental parts to meet special engineering needs and support production. Operate milling equipment, lathes, welding, sheet metal equipment, and other machine tools. Participate in the planning and installation of new equipment, writing and performing of technical procedures and change controls. Complete process improvement projects to increase equipment efficiency, availability, and reliability. Support and meet departmental, plant and corporate HS&E goals. Work in a safe and efficient manner Why you? Basic Qualifications: Associates degree in Electromechanical Technology, Machine Tool Technology, or related field, OR 5 years of manufacturing / packaging equipment maintenance Demonstrated knowledge of and ability to repair and troubleshoot mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems. Demonstrated ability to perform basic electrical repairs like sensor replacements, electrical connections, motor wiring and others. Demonstrated skill in interpreting and applying specifications, blueprints, engineering drawings, and work instructions in order to perform installation, repair, and modification work. Strong computer skills (Word, Excel, Power Point, internet). Good oral and written communication skills. CMMS (Computer Maintenance Management System) knowledge (e.g. SAP). Root Cause Analysis knowledge Preferred Qualifications: Preferred knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing process equipment and systems including automated material handling of solids and liquids, lean manufacturing practices, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) including validation issues and change control processes Experience with mills, lathes and welding is a plus Location – this role is based in: Lincoln, Nebraska. This is not a remote opportunity. Shift: 1st Shift, 6:30am – 3pm Mon-Fri Benefits Haleon offers a robust Total Reward package that consists of competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits program. This includes a generous 401(k) plan, tuition reimbursement and time off programs including 6 months paid parental leave. On day one, you are eligible for benefits, including our healthcare programs where the company pays for the majority of your medical coverage for you and your family. Você atuará em parceria com as áreas de Vendas, Marketing, Finanças, Supply Chain, Categoria, Estratégia Comercial e demais áreas de negócio para identificar oportunidades de crescimento, aprimorar a tomada de decisão, garantir disciplina de preços e maximizar receita líquida, margem e geração de valor no longo prazo. O profissional bem-sucedido deverá adotar uma abordagem estruturada, questionar premissas de forma construtiva, identificar riscos e oportunidades e contribuir para consolidar o Revenue Growth Management como uma capacidade estratégica da organização. Principais responsabilidades Apoiar a implementação e governança das estratégias de Revenue Growth Management nas frentes de precificação, promoções, investimento comercial, condições comerciais, arquitetura de embalagens e preços, mix de portfólio, estratégia de canais e segmentação de clientes. Analisar dados internos e externos, incluindo sell-in, sell-out, participação de mercado, preços, margens, informações de clientes, canais, categorias e concorrentes, identificando oportunidades para aumentar receita, margem e competitividade. Monitorar a execução e conformidade de preços entre clientes, canais, regiões e categorias, identificando desvios das políticas aprovadas e recomendando ações corretivas em conjunto com Vendas e Finanças. Apoiar a definição e evolução contínua de corredores de preço, listas de preços recomendados, estruturas de descontos, diretrizes de investimentos em clientes e controles de perdas de receita. Trabalhar em parceria com as áreas de Vendas, Key Account, Trade Marketing e Clientes para avaliar a efetividade promocional, eficiência dos investimentos comerciais, retorno sobre investimento (ROI), rentabilidade dos clientes e resultados pós-promoção. Apoiar o planejamento promocional, fornecendo recomendações sobre mecânicas promocionais, profundidade de descontos, impactos em volume, margem, riscos de canibalização e viabilidade financeira. Contribuir para processos de planejamento anual, orçamento, forecast, revisões de negócio e gestão de desempenho por meio de análises sobre receita, margem, preços e investimentos comerciais. Desenvolver e aprimorar dashboards, scorecards, relatórios e ferramentas analíticas que possibilitem decisões comerciais mais rápidas e assertivas. Identificar oportunidades de expansão de margem por meio da otimização de preços, melhoria do mix, eficiência dos investimentos comerciais, arquitetura de embalagens, análise de rentabilidade de clientes e redução de perdas de receita. Colaborar com Marketing e Categoria na avaliação do desempenho do portfólio, lançamentos de inovação, evolução do mix de produtos, percepção de valor pelo consumidor e oportunidades para ampliar a rentabilidade das marcas e categorias. Apoiar fóruns de governança multifuncionais por meio da preparação de análises, business cases, recomendações e materiais para tomada de decisão. Monitorar preços da concorrência, dinâmicas de mercado, movimentos dos canais, comportamento dos consumidores, tendências do setor de Consumer Healthcare e fatores macroeconômicos que possam impactar a demanda, rentabilidade e estratégia comercial. Traduzir análises complexas em apresentações executivas claras e objetivas, destacando insights, riscos, oportunidades, recomendações e impactos esperados para o negócio. Garantir alinhamento entre estratégia comercial, metas financeiras, planos de clientes e execução, apoiando decisões equilibradas entre crescimento, rentabilidade, participação de mercado e geração de valor sustentável. Contribuir para melhorias de processos, padronização, desenvolvimento de capacidades e disseminação de melhores práticas de Revenue Growth Management. Atuar como um parceiro analítico confiável para as áreas de negócio, trazendo insights proativamente, desafiando premissas e promovendo decisões baseadas em dados. Por que você? Experiência em Revenue Growth Management, Planejamento Comercial, Sales Finance, Pricing, Trade Marketing, Category Management, Business Intelligence, Business Analytics, Sales Operations ou funções comerciais relacionadas. Forte capacidade analítica, com experiência no tratamento de grandes volumes de dados, identificação de padrões e geração de insights para recomendações comerciais. Conhecimentos avançados em Excel e PowerPoint, com habilidade para desenvolver análises estruturadas, dashboards, business cases e apresentações executivas. Capacidade de gerenciar múltiplas prioridades e cumprir prazos em um ambiente dinâmico. Excelente habilidade de comunicação e gestão de stakeholders, influenciando equipes multifuncionais por meio de recomendações baseadas em dados. Curiosidade para compreender dinâmicas de mercado, comportamento dos clientes e consumidores e desempenho do negócio além dos indicadores numéricos. Inglês avançado ou fluente. Conhecimento das dinâmicas dos canais de farmácias, drogarias, varejo moderno, e-commerce, distribuidores e atacadistas. Experiência apoiando planos anuais de operação, revisões comerciais, fóruns de governança de preços ou análises de investimentos comerciais. Habilidade para construir narrativas executivas (storytelling), simplificando análises complexas para públicos seniores. Alto nível de atenção aos detalhes, senso de dono, resiliência e capacidade de atuar de forma independente. Mentalidade de melhoria contínua e interesse em desenvolver novas ferramentas, processos e capacidades comerciais. Principais interfaces da função Vendas e Key Accounts: planejamento de clientes, execução de preços, efetividade promocional e rentabilidade. Fortalecer a disciplina de preços e a governança de estruturas de descontos e investimentos em clientes. Identificar e quantificar oportunidades para aumentar receita líquida, margem bruta, rentabilidade de clientes e retorno sobre investimentos comerciais. Ele reúne nosso propósito, ambições, direcionadores estratégicos e comportamentos que nos permitem vencer juntos. Esse modelo orienta nossa estratégia, cultura e tomada de decisões. Job Posting About the role To define, maintain and operate enterprise architecture standards, guidance, assurance and governance forums that enable safe, consistent and scalable delivery across D&T, while reducing architectural risk, technical debt and decision ambiguity. Scope (enterprise‑wide, not domain‑specific) This role operates horizontally across all technology and solution domains. It does not design or deliver systems. Core scope areas include (not exhaustive): Enterprise architecture standards and reference architectures Architecture guidance and “minimum viable architecture” guardrails Architecture assurance for programmes, platforms and major investments Architecture governance forums and decision processes Architecture risk, resilience and technical debt reporting Architecture artefacts, documentation and playbooks Key accountabilities The Architecture Assurance, Guidance & Standards Management Lead is accountable for: Defining and maintaining clear, consumable enterprise architecture standards and reference architectures. Operating a consistent architecture assurance model that provides confidence in key initiatives and investments. Chairing and running enterprise architecture governance forums, ensuring decisions are high‑quality, transparent and actionable. Ensuring architecture standards and decisions are applied and followed through, not just agreed. Providing independent architectural risk and resilience insight to senior D&T and governance forums. Key responsibilities 1. Enterprise Architecture Standards & Guardrails Own and maintain enterprise‑wide architecture principles, standards and reference architecture artefacts. Ensure standards are: practical and easy to apply proportionate to risk focused on enablement rather than control for its own sake Regularly refresh standards to reflect changes in platforms, operating model and delivery approach. 2. Architecture Governance Forums (Chairing & Operation) Chair enterprise architecture governance and assurance forums on behalf of the Technology Domain Architect. Set clear agendas aligned to assurance objectives and decision needs. Ensure the right materials are brought forward for decision, not discussion without outcome. Facilitate focused, fact‑based decision‑making and challenge where required. 3. Forum Preparation & Decision Quality Work with architects and delivery teams to prepare architecture submissions for forums, ensuring: decisions are well‑framed options and trade‑offs are clear alignment to standards and principles is explicit Improve the quality and consistency of architectural decision inputs over time. 4. Minutes, Actions & Follow‑Through Capture clear, outcome‑led meeting minutes, including: decisions taken conditions or constraints architecture risks accepted or deferred Track architecture actions arising from forums and ensure accountable owners are assigned. Follow up on actions to ensure decisions are implemented, not forgotten, feeding outcomes back into assurance and standards where necessary. 5. Architecture Assurance Framework Define and operate when and how architecture assurance is required across programmes and investments. Apply assurance proportionately, balancing: speed vs. risk autonomy vs. enterprise consistency Escalate material architecture risks through appropriate governance channels. 6. Risk, Resilience & Technical Debt Insight Aggregate assurance outcomes to provide enterprise‑level visibility of: systemic architectural risk recurring deviations from standards structural resilience and dependency weaknesses Produce concise, decision‑led insights for senior governance forums. 7. “Freedom Within Guardrails” Enablement Translate strategy into minimum viable architectures and guardrails that enable teams to move quickly without repeated escalation. Reduce ambiguity by making “what is allowed” as clear as “what is not”. 8. Architecture Community & Ways of Working Act as a central reference point for architecture governance, standards and assurance guidance across D&T. Coach architects on how to engage effectively with governance forums and assurance processes. Drive continuous improvement of architecture ways of working. What good looks like Architecture forums are well‑run, decision‑focused and respected. Papers are higher quality and require less rework. Decisions are documented, traceable and implemented. Fewer surprises late in delivery due to unresolved architectural risk. Standards evolve based on real delivery feedback, not theoretical design. Qualifications & experience Essential Significant experience in enterprise architecture, architecture governance or assurance roles. Proven experience chairing architecture or technical governance forums. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including clear documentation of decisions and actions. Ability to challenge constructively and maintain independence of judgement. Preferred Experience operating a central architecture assurance or design authority function. Experience in large, global or regulated environments. Skills & capabilities Enterprise‑level architectural judgement Strong facilitation and governance leadership Structured documentation and action tracking Pragmatic, outcome‑focused approach to assurance Why Haleon?
